ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle with F as the center, and G, H, K, M are on the circle. GK is a chord, and the line passing through the center F passes through M, J, H, and intersects the chord GK at J. There is a right-angle mark near J, indicating that this line passing through the center is perpendicular to the chord GK. H is located on the upper minor arc GK corresponding to the chord GK. Then reason: In a circle, a line passing through the center and perpendicular to a chord bisects that chord, and also bisects the arc subtended by that chord. Therefore H is the midpoint of the minor arc GK, so the measures of arc GH and arc HK are equal. It is known that the measure of arc GHK is 142, and arc GHK = arc GH + arc HK, so arc GH = 142 ÷ 2 = 71.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram: F is the center, G and K lie on the circle, GK is a chord, J is where the line FH intersects GK, and the right-angle marker shows FJ is perpendicular to GK. Also H lies on the same ray from F through J. Use FG and FK as radii, so FG = FK, and FJ is common to right triangles FJG and FJK. Because both triangles are right triangles with equal hypotenuses FG and FK and common leg FJ, triangles FJG and FJK are congruent by HL. Thus the central angles on either side of FH are equal: angle GFH = angle HFK. Equal central angles intercept equal arcs, so arc GH = arc HK. From the text, arc GHK measures 142, so arc GH + arc HK = 142; hence each is 71.
